target_statement: For every finite 2-group G in which any two elements with the same normal closure are conjugate, the derived subgroup G' is abelian.

source_clauses.text: Suppose that, in a finite 2-group G, any two elements are conjugate whenever their normal closures coincide. Is it true that the derived subgroup of G is abelian?

constraints.statement: The assertion quantifies over every group G satisfying all remaining admissibility rows.
For all x,y in G, equality of their normal closures <x>^G=<y>^G implies that x and y are conjugate in G.
The derived subgroup G' is abelian, equivalently G''=1.

success_criteria.proof: Prove for every finite 2-group satisfying the exact normal-closure-fibre hypothesis that G''=1.
success_criteria.counterexample: Give a reconstructible finite 2-group satisfying every admissibility row but with G'' nontrivial.
partial_progress: A proved structural restriction on a minimum counterexample.
An independently reproducible exhaustive finite-order exclusion with its exact coverage stated.
success_criteria.certificate: A line-by-line proof, or an explicit presentation/library identifier with independent checks of every normal-closure fibre and of G'' nontrivial.

truth_likelihood.rationale: Planning estimate: the hypothesis is exceptionally rigid and earlier bounded exploration did not expose a witness; the estimate is not a verdict.

priority.rationale: The property is exact and admits both structural reductions and bounded independent checks.
